title: Hull-House, 1913: the Week Chicago Lined Up to See a 'Devil Baby'

sources.what: 'For a period of six weeks in the fall of 1913, thousands of people appeared at Hull-House'; versions by immigrant group
'his cloven hoofs, his pointed ears and diminutive tail'; visitors 'poured in all day long'
sources.who: Jane Addams, 'The Devil Baby at Hull-House,' The Atlantic, Oct. 1916 (Ramapo digital edition)

sources.what: devil baby legend; people lined up; Hull House rumored to be the dwelling of spirits
'No amount of denial convinced them that he was not there'; Lady in White lore; ghost tours
Chicago Examiner, Halloween 1913: thousands believed it

beats.text: In 1913, crowds lined up in Chicago to see a devil baby.
beats.label: CHICAGO, 1913
beats.credit: History: Jane Addams Papers Project; WTTW

beats.text: The rumor said a baby with hooves and a tail was hidden at Hull-House, Jane Addams's settlement house on Halsted Street.
beats.label: HULL-HOUSE

beats.text: For six weeks, people streamed in from all over the city, asking to see it.
beats.label: SIX WEEKS
beats.credit: Jane Addams Papers Project; Hull-House Museum

beats.text: Addams said there was no such baby. They didn't believe her.
beats.label: JANE ADDAMS

beats.text: Each immigrant group told its own version of the story.
beats.label: THE STORIES
beats.credit: Jane Addams Papers Project; The Atlantic (1916)

beats.text: There never was a devil baby. But legend says Hull-House is haunted anyway.
beats.label: THE LEGEND

beats.text: Today it's a museum, open to the public.
beats.label: TODAY

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck.result: 'thousands lined up' became 'crowds lined up'; 'all day long' became 'streamed in from all over the city'; versions by immigrant group, not neighborhood; quote exact (Addams, Atlantic, 1916); all supported
